Empirical Research Plan: 65‐Year-Old Medicare Eligibility and Hospital Utilization  

------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy  
------------------------------------------------------------------
Method: Sharp Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD).  
Rationale:  
• The “running” (assignment) variable—exact age in years (or quarters)—is continuous and impossible to manipulate strategically.  
• At the legislated cutoff of 65, Medicare eligibility (and therefore insurance coverage) jumps discretely from ≈86–88 % to ≈98–99 % while nothing else, by law, changes discontinuously at that exact birthday.  
• The causal estimand is the local average treatment effect (LATE) of (near-)universal insurance on outcomes measured very close to age 65.  
• Both the NHIS and hospital discharge files contain exact age, making it feasible to implement nonparametric local‐linear RDD à la Imbens & Kalyanaraman (2012) or Calonico, Cattaneo & Titiunik (2014).  

------------------------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control Definition  
------------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
• Dᵢ = 1 if individual i is age ≥65 (eligible for Medicare), 0 otherwise.  

Control group  
• Individuals just below the cutoff (e.g., 60–64.99 years or, in the RD window, 64 ⅟₂–65 years) serve as counterfactuals for those just above 65.  

Timing / Event  
• Event date = 65th birthday; utilization measured at the discharge date (NIS/OSHPD) or interview date (NHIS) expressed in age in days/quarters.  

Running variable & cutoff  
• Xᵢ = exact age in days (preferred) or quarters relative to 65.  
• Cutoff c = 0 (i.e., Xᵢ = 0 on 65th birthday).  
• Use h on each side of the cutoff (data-driven bandwidth selection).  

------------------------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions  
------------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Continuity of potential outcomes at age 65 absent treatment.  
  Plausibility: Health status evolves smoothly with age; no other federal program changes exactly at the 65th birthday (Social Security’s Full Retirement Age >65 for these cohorts).  

A2. No manipulation of the running variable.  
  Plausibility: Individuals cannot misreport or alter date of birth on administrative hospital data.  

A3. Stable composition of cohorts locally.  
  Plausibility: Mortality around 65 is low; migration unlikely to sort around exact birthdays.  

A4. First stage is strong and discontinuous.  
  Empirically testable in NHIS: coverage jumps ≈85–90 pp at 65.  

------------------------------------------------------------------
4. Threats to Identification & Mitigation  
------------------------------------------------------------------
T1. Concurrent retirement effects (labor supply withdrawal ⇒ more time to seek care).  
  Mitigation:  
  • Show labor‐force participation from CPS/ACS is smooth at exact 65 (the statutory FRA was 65 + 2–4 months for these cohorts).  
  • Control for employment status in NHIS subsample; replicate RD in California where state pension rules do not kink at 65.  

T2. Age heaping/measurement error (e.g., age coded in years only).  
  Mitigation:  
  • Use age in days/quarters when possible; in year-only files restrict to ±6-month window and implement McCrary density test on age in days (OSHPD keeps DOB).  

T3. Differential coding or reporting by Medicare payers post-65 (Medicare as primary payer influences DRG coding).  
  Mitigation:  
  • Focus on count of admissions, not charges or DRG weights.  
  • Use “all-payer” admission counts (regardless of payer) to show similar qualitative results.  

------------------------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline (execut­able)  
------------------------------------------------------------------
```r
# Required libraries
library(data.table)   # Fast reading
library(fixest)       # Regressions
library(rdrobust)     # RD estimators
library(ggplot2)      # Plots

# 1. Load data (example: CA discharges)
os <- fread("OSHPD_1992_2002.csv")      # large file; pre-cleaned
pop <- fread("Census_single_age_CA.csv")

# 2. Variable construction
# Convert DOB and admit date to decimal age
os[, age_days := as.numeric(admit_date - dob)]
os[, age_years := age_days / 365.25]
# Running variable: centered at 65th birthday
os[, runvar := age_years - 65]

# Treatment indicator
os[, treat65 := as.integer(runvar >= 0)]

# Outcome: hospital utilization per capita
# Collapse to cell-level (age in 0.1‐year bins)
os[, bin := round(runvar, 1)]
admits <- os[, .N, by = bin]            # Number of discharges
setkey(pop, age_year)
setkey(admits, bin)
admits <- pop[admits, on = .(age_year = bin)]
admits[, admit_rate := N / population]  # per capita

# 3. Main RD regression (local linear, IK bandwidth)
rd_main <- rdrobust(y = admits$admit_rate,
                    x = admits$bin, p = 1, kernel = "triangular")

summary(rd_main)

# 4. Graphical RD plot
ggplot(admits, aes(x = bin, y = admit_rate)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_smooth(data = admits[bin >= -3 & bin <= 3],
              method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE, color = "blue") +
  labs(x = "Age relative to 65 (years)",
       y = "Admissions per capita",
       title = "Hospital Admissions Around Medicare Eligibility")

# 5. Robustness: alternative bandwidth (±1.5 years)
rd_small <- rdrobust(y = admits$admit_rate,
                     x = admits$bin, p = 1, h = 1.5, kernel = "triangular")
summary(rd_small)
```
(Analogous code for NHIS first-stage on insurance coverage.)  

------------------------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results (Prior)  
------------------------------------------------------------------
Direction: Positive. Obtaining coverage eliminates price barriers, leading to more inpatient admissions.  
Magnitude (back-of-the-envelope):  
• Pre-65 admission rate ~180 per 1,000 persons annually.  
• Expect ~5–8 % jump ⇒ +9–15 admissions per 1,000.  
• Corresponds to RD coefficient of ≈0.009–0.015 admissions per capita.  

------------------------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (RDD)  
------------------------------------------------------------------
C1: No manipulation of running variable (McCrary density test) … 1  
C2: Covariate balance at cutoff (gender, race, pre-existing trends) … 1  
C3: Continuity of outcome in absence of treatment … 0.8 (cannot prove)  
C4: Robust to bandwidths / polynomial order … 1  
C5: Placebo tests at other cutoffs (e.g., 60, 62, 68) … 1  

Overall score: 4.8 / 5 → high internal validity.
